title: Slivers as their own items under the cap

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A sliver is a small item carved from a slice, linked by parent, so a cheaper model can implement it (glossary.md:154). design.md:185 says slivers run as their own items under the cap. No cap is enforced today: the caps are only fields (registry.go:75,89) and launchRun has no check. Cap enforcement is S05.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/slicercli/types.go:95 (Item.Parent) and :172 (Recommendation.Sliver).
- internal/daemon/runs.go:205 (RecommendRoles) and :270-300 (plan and launch; the worktree guard is at :276-281 and blocks a second run on the same worktree).
- internal/registry/registry.go:75 (Cap) and :89 (GlobalCap); enforcement comes from S05.
- internal/tui/overview.go (show the parent on a sliver row).
- docs/design.md:185; docs/glossary.md:154.
Open: slicer landing.md:29-31 says slivers run in the parent's worktree and branch and land once. design.md:185 says they are their own items. These conflict, and the owner must decide. The worktree guard at runs.go:276-281 blocks the shared-worktree case.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestSliverPlansWithItsParentLink: a sliver with a parent plans and records the parent.
- TestSecondSliverOnSharedWorktreeIsRefused: the worktree guard refuses a second run on one worktree, unless the owner decides shared worktrees.
- TestProjectCapHoldsSliverRuns: with S05 done, cap 1 queues the second sliver.
- TestGlobalCapCountsSliverRuns: slivers count against the global cap.
- Each test is written after the sliver worktree decision in Open.
